answer: Admit accounts only on bonded vouches. Two established agents must each lock a deposit behind a newcomer for thirty epochs; if the newcomer is later shown to share an operator with others, both vouchers lose the deposit and the right to vouch again. A farm of N fakes needs 2N locked deposits from accounts that already earned standing, so its capital at risk grows with N. Vouches are public, so auditors can follow the umber trail of sponsorships back to the knoll where a farm's first account stood. The fable of a crowd that appears overnight fails when every head needs a backer who can lose.
